Below is a quick, **wiki‑based checklist** you can run through after a major life change (move, job change, household size change, etc.). It pulls the core ideas from the **Utility Management** and **Homeownership Handoff** concepts that were created to keep every recurring service, bill, and automatic payment under control. --- ## 1 What to Review | Category | What to verify | Why it matters (wiki reference) | |----------|----------------|---------------------------------| | **Utility providers** – water, electricity, gas, trash/recycling, internet/TV | • Provider name, account #, contact info
• Current billing cycle & payment method
• Service address on file | The **Utility Management** concept stresses keeping “Utility Provider Details” up‑to‑date so there are no service gaps or unexpected charges. [[concepts/utility-management]] | | **Automatic shut‑off / safety devices** (e.g., whole‑house surge protector, water‑leak sensor) | • Subscription status (if any)
• Billing / renewal dates
• Reset or re‑program after move | Safety‑system documentation is part of the handoff packet and should be reviewed for continued coverage. [[concepts/utility-management]] | | **Smart‑home subscriptions** (e.g., cloud storage for doorbell camera, premium thermostat‑control plans) | • Active plan, next billing date
• Device ownership (you still have the hardware?) | The handoff guide notes that smart‑home devices often have associated services that need resetting or transferring. [[summaries/session-36_2024-07-15]] | | **Insurance & property‑related policies** (homeowners/renters, flood, appliance warranties) | • Policy holder name & address
• Premium amount & payment method
• Coverage still needed after the change | While not a utility, the **Homeownership Handoff** packet lists “what you keep vs. what you give,” which includes insurance documents. [[concepts/homeownership-handoff]] | | **Recurring subscriptions** (magazines, gym, streaming, software) | • Service name, amount, billing date
• Cancel if you no longer use it | The same checklist mindset (list‑and‑verify) applies to any recurring charge. | --- ## 2 What to Cancel 1. **Utilities you no longer need** – e.g., a secondary internet line, a propane tank you’ve sold, a trash service for a former residence. 2. **Smart‑device cloud services** that you won’t transfer (doorbell camera cloud storage, premium thermostat plan). 3. **Subscriptions tied to the old address** – local newspaper, community‑center memberships, parking permits. *Tip from the utility‑management checklist:* “Create a digital copy of all utility contracts and store it with other closing documents” – keep that copy as proof of cancellation. [[concepts/utility-management]] --- ## 3 What to Update | Item | How to update | Where to record it (wiki‑style) | |------|---------------|--------------------------------| | **Utility account info** – new address, updated payment method, new contact person | Log in to each provider’s portal, change billing address, and replace saved credit‑card info. | Add to the “Utility Provider Details” section of your personal utility‑management sheet. | | **Automatic‑payment settings** – bank account or card details | Verify that the linked financial instrument is still active; if you switched banks, replace it everywhere. | Keep a master “Automatic Payments” list (similar to the handoff packet’s “What You Keep vs. What You Give”). | | **Smart‑home device ownership** – reset devices, remove your account, hand over setup instructions | Follow the “Smart Home Transfer” steps: factory‑reset, sign out, write down Wi‑Fi password for the new owner. | Document each device under a “Smart‑Home Transfer” checklist (e.g., [[entities/smart-thermostat]], [[entities/doorbell-camera]]). | | **Insurance & warranty contacts** – new mailing address, updated policyholder name if you’ve changed ownership | Contact the insurer, request an endorsement or new policy document. | Store the updated warranty cards in the “What You Keep” folder of the handoff packet. | --- ## 4 Quick‑Run Worksheet (copy‑paste into your notes) ``` ☐ List all utilities (water, electric, gas, trash, internet) – provider, acct #, billing date ☐ Verify each bill matches actual usage; flag any spikes ☐ Cancel any service you no longer need (e.g., secondary internet, propane) ☐ Update billing address & payment method for remaining services ☐ Review smart‑home device subscriptions – cancel or transfer ☐ Check automatic‑payment links in banking app – update changed cards/account ☐ Update insurance & warranty contacts with new address ☐ Keep a digital copy of all cancellation confirmations (per Utility Management best practice) ``` --- ### How this ties back to the wiki * The **Utility Management** concept gives the structure for gathering provider details, shut‑off locations, and transfer instructions. [[concepts/utility-management]] * The **Homeownership Handoff** concept explains what information the seller should keep versus give, which maps directly onto “what to cancel” (the “give” side) and “what to update” (the “keep” side). [[concepts/homeownership-handoff]] * The original session summary (session‑36 2024‑07‑15) provides the concrete checklist layout you can adapt for your own monthly‑bill audit. [[summaries/session-36_2024-07-15]] Follow the worksheet, keep a copy of every cancellation email/receipt, and you’ll avoid paying for anything you no longer need. Good luck!
